blocks.heading: Route By Route
rows: Employers pay for people who can trace a fraud pattern. They hire on a skills test and proof of cases analysed, not on a criminology degree.
SQL or Excel depth, basic accounting or IT, plus criminology as the context layer.
Scalable with a business layer NCRB recorded 86,420 cyber crime cases in 2023, about 69% of them fraud. Fraud-analysis skill can later be sold as consulting or training.
Corporate risk, fraud and due-diligence work
Companies and law firms pay for checks on partners, staff and suppliers.
A law, commerce or data base, a clear writing sample, and references.
Research, policy briefs and crime-data writing (think tanks, NGOs, your own newsletter)
Foundations, think tanks and media pay for clear analysis of public data.
Statistics, plain writing and a public body of work.
Paid research and training come from that audience.
Training and awareness sessions (cyber fraud, child safety, workplace safety)
Schools, companies and housing societies pay for sessions that are clear and local.
A tested talk, a simple offer and one or two local references.
Prison, probation and correctional services
State governments. Posts and qualification rules are set by each state.
State recruitment rules. Some state notices accept social work, psychology or related degrees. Read the qualification line in each one.
Not so scalable NCRB counted 1,468 sanctioned correctional posts and 820 filled at the end of 2022. The need is real, but pay follows a fixed government scale.
State police and CAPF officer exams
Central and state governments, through public service commissions and UPSC.
A general graduate degree and a competitive exam. UPSC CAPF (Assistant Commandant) 2026 listed 349 posts for ages 20 to 25.
Not so scalable Several filters in a row (written test, physical test, interview, then promotion). Criminology is not the entry key.

blocks.heading: Degrees and Institutes, with Entry Rules
rows: NFSU (National Forensic Sciences University)
B.Sc. Criminology and Forensic Science, 3 years. Campuses listed for 2026-27: Gandhinagar, Delhi, Chennai.
Class 12 science with 55% (50% for SC, ST, PwD). Admission through CUET-UG 2026.
Tuition Rs 65,000 per semester, so Rs 3.9 lakh over six semesters, before hostel and exams.
A blend of lab and social science. Choose the M.A. below if you want the social-science side without the lab.
NFSU
M.A. Criminology, 2 years (Gandhinagar and Delhi). Also M.A. Police and Security Studies and M.Sc. Forensic Psychology.
CUET-PG 2026, Criminology paper code SCQP10 for the M.A.
Tuition Rs 60,000 per semester for the M.A., so Rs 2.4 lakh over four semesters.
Costly against a Rs 10 lakh education budget (24%). Ask for verified placement roles, not a brochure line.
NFSU
LL.M. (Criminal Law and Criminal Justice Administration), 1 year. LL.M. (Cyber Law and Cyber Crime Investigation), 1 year.
Three-year LL.B. or five-year integrated law degree with 50%, plus PG-CLAT 2026.
Law plus criminology is the strongest pairing for prosecution support, compliance and cyber-crime work.
Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), Gujarat
M.A./M.Sc. Criminology and Crime Science, a hybrid version, LL.M. in Criminal and Security Laws, and a Master's in Financial and Economic Crimes with IICA.
Listed on the 2026 admissions notice. Eligibility and fees are not stated there, so check rru.ac.in.
Check the RRU brochure.
The financial-crimes master's matches the fastest-growing route. Ask what its graduates actually do.
TISS Mumbai
M.A. Social Work (Criminology and Justice), 4 semesters, 80 credits, 30 seats.
Check the current TISS selection page. Sources disagree on the test.
Total course fees Rs 1,63,900 on the TISS page, with fieldwork and study tour paid separately.
Fieldwork in all four semesters and a research project. Strongest for correctional, juvenile justice and NGO routes.
Ambedkar University Delhi
M.A. Criminology.
Admission through CUET-PG. The 2023-24 listing asked for a bachelor's degree in any discipline with 55%. Confirm the 2026-27 brochure.
Check the brochure.
This is Ambedkar University Delhi, not Delhi University.

blocks.heading: Is Criminology a Good Career
rows: You picture detective work and profiling
India has no large employer base for profilers. Most criminology work is reading data, writing reports and handling files. Test that daily work before you pay for it.
You need a fixed salary within a year of graduating
No post is reserved for criminology graduates. The first job usually comes from a second skill, an internship, or an exam that does not ask for criminology at all.
You dislike statistics and long reports
Every paid route here runs on numbers or written analysis. A student who avoids both will struggle in the degree and in the job.
You want lab work on DNA, toxicology or digital evidence
That is forensic science, a different degree with a different entry requirement. Read the forensic science verdict instead.
You want to be a licensed counsellor or clinical psychologist
That path runs through psychology and a licensing board. Criminology is a side layer there.
